description: Known-malware indicators for the on-device virus scanner: Android malware families spread to users in Uzbekistan and the CIS through Telegram. Every value is copied verbatim from the public report cited in its family's "sources" (lower-cased, filed by hash length); nothing is inferred, completed or invented. A match is treated as decisive (MALICIOUS), so an indicator is only added when the report attributes it to a malware sample, and a package name only when it cannot plausibly be a legitimate app's id. "published", "notes" and "sample_filenames" are provenance for maintainers; the parser ignores them. This file is copied byte-identical to SkySecure TMessagesProj/src/main/assets/device-threat-intel.json.

families.name: Ajina.Banker
families.notes: SMS-stealing banker spread through Telegram chats in Uzbekistan and Central Asia. Hashes: all 1,628 rows of the report's "Indicators of compromise" table (md5/sha1/sha256 of the same samples), plus the SHA-1 of the "Вип Контент.apk" sample cited in the text. Package org.zzzz.aaa is named in the report as the package of 1,215 samples. com.example.smshandler (187 samples) is deliberately NOT listed: it is Android Studio's default id for any project called "SMS Handler", so a match would be a decisive false accusation against a developer's own build; the published samples that used it are covered by their hashes. Not listed either: SHA-1 1a9c98808a547d4b50cc31d46e19045bcd2cfc1b (an HTTP response-body hash of the gate panel, not a sample) and the network indicators.

families.name: Qwizzserial
families.notes: SMS stealer spread through Telegram in Uzbekistan (~100,000 infections) under lures such as "Moliyaviy Yordam" and "Presidential Support". Hashes: all 1,190 rows of the report's "Indicators of Compromise (IOCs) / Files" table (sha256/sha1/md5 of the same samples). The report names no Android package ids ("Qwizzserial" is the Java package of the main activity, shared across samples with different package names).

families.name: Wonderland
families.notes: Two-way (WebSocket C2) SMS stealer, formerly tracked as WretchedCat, spread in Uzbekistan from stolen Telegram sessions. Every row of the report's "Indicators of Compromise (IOCs) / File Hashes" table attributed to Wonderland (SHA-1 only; the report publishes no other hash type and no package names — it says the operators rotate package names, sometimes daily).

families.name: MidnightDat
families.notes: Dropper that carries the stealer payload in an encrypted .dat asset and installs it through a PackageInstaller session. Every row of the report's "Indicators of Compromise (IOCs) / File Hashes" table attributed to MidnightDat (SHA-1 only; the report publishes no other hash type and no package names — it says the operators rotate package names, sometimes daily).

families.name: RoundRift
families.notes: Dropper that decrypts an embedded payload from a [name].key asset. Every row of the report's "Indicators of Compromise (IOCs) / File Hashes" table attributed to RoundRift (SHA-1 only; the report publishes no other hash type and no package names — it says the operators rotate package names, sometimes daily).

families.name: Mamont
families.notes: Banking trojan (Trojan-Banker.AndroidOS.Mamont) delivered from a Telegram chat as a fake parcel-tracking app. The one file hash in the report's "Indicators of compromise" (MD5). The C2 host is not a device indicator and is not listed.
